size.note: Newman's Birds gives 23–24 cm. Wikipedia gives 23 cm.

habitat: Well-developed woodland and mixed bushveld, especially tall riverine Acacia stands and Mopane, and riverine or swamp-fringing woodland. Often far from water. Hunts from an exposed perch.
summary: A loud summer visitor with an electric turquoise back, black shoulders, whitish head and underparts, a black stripe from the bill through the eye, and a bill red above and black below. The trilling song is a familiar Kruger summer sound. Dark grey legs are from Wikipedia only. Newman's says the immature bill is usually red, sometimes with a black tip; Wikipedia says brown, and a Kruger photograph shows a dark bill.

similar.note: Brown-hooded has a wholly red bill, a streaked brown head and buffy, streaked underparts (Newman's).
Striped also has a two-tone bill but is smaller and grey-brown, with a black eye-stripe round the nape (Newman's).
Grey-headed has an all-red bill, a grey head and a chestnut belly (Newman's).

bill.shape: Newman's says the immature bill is usually all red, sometimes with a black tip. Wikipedia says brown. A Kruger photograph shows a dark bill.

viewNotes.note: Front-on, the clean white underparts and head, and the red-over-black bill (eBird; Newman's).
Side-on, the black stripe from bill to ear-coverts and the two-tone bill (Newman's).
From behind, the electric turquoise-blue back contrasts with the black shoulders (Newman's; eBird).
White underwing-coverts and black flight feathers (Wikipedia). The wing-spread display shows the same pattern; it is not a flight shot.
From above, the blue back and wing panel show against the black coverts (Wikipedia). The display photograph shows this upperwing; it is not a flight shot.

calls.description: A loud 'yimp-trrrrrrrrrr', the last part drawn out and descending, sometimes given with the wings extended (Newman's; eBird). Newman's says the male gives this continuously after arrival until breeding ends. No different female song is described, and some recordings are of pairs, so it is not stored as a male-only song.
An alarm call, from a recording the recordist labelled as an alarm. The field-guide texts used here do not describe it.
